generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the broadleaf base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the broadleaf program gave as defaults until then.

traits.perianth.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 315: perianth lacking, uniseriate or biseriate (formula K 0-8, C 0-8); Floral Diagrams p. 257: calyx valvate, corolla rare, perianth reduced to glands in Salix and Populus.

traits.flower_merosity.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 256, 257: merism variable, general formula 3 to 7 or more sepals; Simpson p. 315 allows up to 15. Simpson's rare 15 is capped at the vocabulary's 12.

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 315, 505: Simpson calls the flowers hypogynous; Floral Diagrams p. 257 adds that a hypanthium is often developed in the former Flacourtiaceae (e.g. Casearia).

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 57 Salicaceae (the willows and poplars): trees or shrubs; leaves alternate, simple; stipules small or leafy; flowers on separate trees, in catkins, with no perianth; ovary superior; fruit a capsule of many hairy seeds. APG's Salicaceae also holds most of the old Flacourtiaceae, trees and shrubs with alternate simple leaves and flowers with a perianth, often also on separate plants; their catkins, missing perianths and capsules belong to the willows' and poplars' genus files.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Salicaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Scyphostegiaceae: how long the leaves last (character 37), coded deciduous. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.
